subject: MSA + Order Form redlines — product rights, training, and feedback license

Subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — IP & Training

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team attached redlines to the MSA and Order Form focusing on the sections that touch on productization, output ownership, and training. High level:
- Zephyr needs clarity that customer output is owned by Zephyr and cannot be used by Redwood to further train models unless we opt in and are compensated.
- We propose a narrow feedback license limited to safety/security improvements and with strict de-identification.
- We asked for an explicit carveout preventing Redwood from using any Zephyr PII or proprietary prompts for model retraining.

I attached the redline PDF for reference (Zephyr_Redlines_MSA_OrderForm_20270831.pdf). Can we schedule a 30-min call this week to walk through? We are hoping to finalize before procurement signs off.

Best,

Subject: FW: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — negotiation levers

Lauren / Marissa —

Quick internal note after skimming Arianna's redlines:
- Sales priority: keep Zephyr on hosted Dedicated plan; anything that forces us to remove telemetry/feedback reduces product ops value. Our suggested negotiation levers:
  * Allow output ownership for Zephyr, but keep a narrow productization exception for aggregated, non-attributable evaluation metrics (no retrain on raw prompts).
  * Introduce an opt-in paid "model-improvement" program (50% credit for first year) that explicitly requires signed opt-in form per dataset.
  * Limit any feedback license to anonymized telemetry and quality-of-service improvement only.
- Risk: Zephyr's proposed blanket ban on "proprietary prompts" could be operationally impossible to enforce without heavy SLO impacts. We should push for definitional clarity instead.

I've drafted some talking points and a short response doc — attaching: Redwood_Proposed_Response_20270903.docx. Please review and add legal redlines.

Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — legal suggestions

Lauren / Ben —

I reviewed Zephyr's PDF and Ben's draft. Proposed positions and concrete language below (high level):
1) Output ownership: agree that Zephyr owns direct customer output. We will accept assignment for product output, with a clarified definition of "derived from" that excludes generic model improvements and aggregated metrics. Suggested clause: "Customer Output means content generated by the Service in response to Customer Input; Redwood shall not assert ownership of Customer Output."
2) Training/data use: carve a limited, optional "Training Opt-In" in the Order Form. We propose a two-tier approach:
   - Default: No use of Customer Input, Customer Output, or proprietary prompts for model training.
   - Optional: Customer may opt in to the Training Opt-In addendum to allow use for explicit, narrowly scoped model tuning; Redwood must document dataset, retention window, and provide compensation (credits or discount).
3) Feedback license: revise to a narrow, perpetual-but-nonexclusive license only for service reliability, model safety fixes, and operational telemetry, not for productization. Add de-identification obligations and prohibit use for generative model training unless opted-in.

I attached a redline-ready PDF for Redwood's response (Redwood_Response_Redlines_20270905.pdf). I flagged several Zephyr edits where we should either accept or propose the opt-in path.

If we're aligned on the opt-in structure I can convert to tracked Word and we'll push during the call.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi Arianna —

Thanks for the redlines and for the patience while we reviewed. Attaching our proposed response that maps to each Zephyr edit and offers a practical opt-in path for training (Redwood_Response_Redlines_20270905.pdf). High-level summary:
- We accept Zephyr ownership of Customer Output.
- We propose default prohibition of use of Customer Input/Output for model training unless Zephyr signs the Training Opt-In addendum (scope + credits).
- Feedback license: restricted to service safety/stability and aggregated telemetry; no use for product model training without opt-in.

Next steps: please review the attached redline and choose a time on my calendar if you'd like to talk through specific clauses: https://calendly.com/lauren_bishop/zephyr-redlines-30m. If procurement is ready, we can ship the revised documents to them for redline acceptance and move to DocuSign.
